unit.why: A short deathbed anecdote, quoted from the preface of ספר ד״ש: R. Mordechai of Lechovitch travels to a wedding, dies in Stolin, and before his passing holds his tzitzit and recites a verse.
unit.boundary_note: the division ends with the section marker 'סליק אות צ ונתחיל אות ק' and the heading 'מענין קבלת שבת', which belongs to the next division

stories.start_quote: ונסע זקני הק׳ מהר"ם ז״ל מלעכוויטש
stories.end_quote: אשר שם בבשרינו ויש בזה סוד
stories.summary_en: R. Mordechai of Lechovitch travelled to a wedding and died in Stolin; before his death he held his tzitzit and recited 'El Hai Helkenu…' from the circumcision blessing, in which there is a secret.

tags.why: The whole anecdote is the tzaddik's deathbed scene and last words.

quotes: ונח נפשיה בשם ומנו״כ בעיר סטאלין
שקודם הסתלקותו אחז את הציצית בידו
ונסע זקני הק׳ מהר"ם ז״ל מלעכוויטש על החתונה
tags.why: He died away from home, at Stolin, while travelling to a wedding.
A wedding is the occasion of the journey.
The narrator says his last words hold a hidden mystical meaning.

quotes: אל חי חלקנו צורנו צוה להציל ידידות שארינו
tags.why: He recites a liturgical blessing as his final words.
